scope: Backlog 2 Batch 022 — fixed membership S3577, S4961, S4806, S3219, S5338
model: GPT-5.6 Sol (medium); documented local substitute because the skill-default GPT-5.5 was unavailable in this workspace.

checks: Each attached primary PDF was inspected once; the live primary-file SHA-256 matched the downloaded source for every fixed member.

S3577 was classified as an overlapping secondary analysis of the already-live S344 Qatar Stars League cohort; S4806 was classified as a systematic review. Neither is staged as a new primary-cohort extraction.

S4961, S3219, and S5338 have a direct at-risk denominator or a directly reported accepted incidence denominator. No exposure, count, rate, burden, or time-loss value was back-calculated from another metric.
Tabs 1–4 were staged for each primary-cohort payload; Tables, results text, and usable figures were swept for Tabs 5–10. Structured fields use source-row-aligned population values.

Field identifiers, two-line population alignment, and source-to-payload values will be validated locally before apply. The generic apply-script dry run cannot simulate new multiline groups before population sync, so it is intentionally not used as a false assurance.

exclusions.flagReason: Secondary analysis of existing S344 Qatar Stars League 2013/14-2014/15 cohort; not independently extracted
caveats: The paper explicitly describes itself as a secondary analysis of the 2013-2015 Qatar Stars League prospective cohort.
The parent cohort is already live as S344 (Epidemiology of time loss groin injuries in a men's professional football league: a 2-year prospective study of 17 clubs and 606 players).
No independent extraction is staged, avoiding duplicate cohort counting while retaining this fixed Batch 022 member and its attached source.

exclusions.flagReason: Systematic review/meta-analysis; not a primary extraction record
caveats: PRISMA systematic review of five controlled trials; the narrative synthesis is not a primary surveillance cohort.

studyDetails.title: Incidence and risk factors of spondylolysis in youth football: a longitudinal study among male Norwegian players.

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [MRI-confirmed spondylolysis after low-back-pain clinical criteria]
definitions.incidenceDefinition: MRI-confirmed spondylolysis cases per 1000 training and match hours
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: same site on follow-up MRI; different side or level classified as new
definitions.mechanismReporting: player self-report with physiotherapist clinical follow-up

caveats: The paper reports a direct incidence denominator but not total season-wide player-hours; no exposure was inferred from the rate.
It is a specific spondylolysis cohort, so the target diagnosis is retained only in the structured diagnosis row and is not echoed as a most-common all-injury outcome.
No direct anatomical-region count is reported for defensible location-tab mapping.

caveats: Table 2 phase counts and the Results text support 56 UEFA plus 29 Copa new injuries (85 total); Table 4's location spectrum instead totals 56 plus 30. The headline outcome preserves the former while direct Table 4 location rows are retained as printed for reviewer attention.
The paper gives incompatible UEFA match-rate text values (15.3 in Results versus 17.1 in Discussion); the Results value 15.3 is retained. Copa's direct 18.7 is retained.

The stored time-loss total/burden use Table 3's overall-impact values that include post-tournament days (1633/558 days; burden 167.0/98.0). The separately reported tournament-only burden (30.4/17.6) has no second compatible headline field and is retained in this caveat for review.

Figure 4 is readable: hamstring counts (9/7) are percentage-derived from the directly stated muscle-injury denominators (35/15). Figure 2 is combined-by-phase only and is not falsely assigned to the two tournament rows. Back and lower-leg/Achilles labels without an exact narrower location mapping remain limited to defensible parent rows.
